# MNNV — Self-Learning Plugin for MiniMax Code

The brain is a real 3D scene at <http://localhost:6789/neural.html>, backed by a
zero-dependency Node server in `plugins/brain/`. It indexes every action,
weights every concept, evolves L1 atoms → L2 scenarios → L3 personas, and lets
the user edit any neuron's wiki card. The edit takes effect on the very next
retrieval — no restart.

## Mental model

Everything in the brain is a **neuron** (an OKF card with an id, a weight, a
vector, and edges to other neurons). Six **lobes** group them by role:

- `l0`      — Conversation log (every user message, tool call, outcome).
- `chatmem` — L1 atoms: preferences, facts, decisions, corrections.
- `skills`  — Reusable procedures (howto / pattern cards).
- `wiki`    — Reference knowledge (decision / reference / gotcha cards).
- `code`    — CodeGraph (symbols, callers, file paths).
- `feedback`— Contradiction, supersedes, deprecate, weight deltas.

A central **Memory Coordinator** sphere sits in the middle. Lobes orbit it.
Neurons orbit their lobe. Edges are synapses; thickness = weight.

## When to use this skill

Trigger this skill automatically when the user (or you) does any of:

- Says "remember this", "save that", "that's a preference", "use this from now on".
- Says "search my memory", "what do I know about X", "find me a similar pattern".
- Says "edit the wiki", "open the wiki for X", "fix that card".
- Asks the brain to do anything: `/brain start`, `/brain stop`, `/brain status`.
- Makes a tool call — every tool call is logged through the brain automatically
  once `/brain start` has been run, so the brain watches the activity.jsonl
  sidecar file.

Do **not** use this skill for: ordinary chat that doesn't need persistence,
ephemeral file edits, or one-off web fetches.

## Tools (call via the brain's HTTP API)

The brain exposes a small, fast HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:6789`. Always call it —
never read JSONL files directly from inside this skill, because the brain
maintains the indexes and weights atomically.

Base URL: `http://127.0.0.1:6789`. All bodies are JSON. All responses are JSON
unless the path is `.html`.

| Method | Path                      | Purpose                                  |
|--------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| GET    | `/api/health`             | `{ok, version, uptime_s, atoms, edges}`  |
| POST   | `/api/atoms`              | Create a new L1 atom (returns id)        |
| GET    | `/api/atoms/:id`          | Read a single atom                       |
| PATCH  | `/api/atoms/:id`          | Edit atom (title, body, tags)            |
| POST   | `/api/atoms/:id/supersede`| Mark old atom as superseded, link new    |
| POST   | `/api/search`             | `{q, k?, lobe?}` → ranked neuron list    |
| POST   | `/api/feedback`           | Record user correction, boost β         |
| GET    | `/api/activity?n=200`     | Recent activity log                      |
| GET    | `/api/evolve/proposals`   | L2 / L3 distillation proposals           |
| POST   | `/api/evolve/accept/:id`  | Accept a proposal (creates new atom)     |
| POST   | `/api/evolve/dismiss/:id` | Dismiss a proposal                       |
| GET    | `/api/graph`              | Full graph for the 3D scene              |
| GET    | `/wiki/:id`               | Editable HTML page for one neuron        |

## How to log a tool call

After **every** tool call (read, write, edit, glob, grep, bash, task,
web_search, etc.), append one JSON line to the inbox log. The brain
tails this file every 500ms and treats each line as an event — the same
path the live HTTP endpoint takes, so the SSE stream and the neural
pulses fire identically.

```
File:  C:\Users\ThePa\.minimax\plugins\brain\data\inbox.log
Mode:  append
Line:  one JSON object, single line, \n terminator
```

Body shape:

```json
{
  "kind": "tool",
  "tool": "<tool name>: read | write | edit | glob | grep | bash | ...",
  "args_summary": "<short summary of what you did>",
  "result_kind": "ok|err",
  "tokens": ["rust","cargo","build"],
  "duration_ms": 1234
}
```

The `tokens` field is what the brain's vector index uses to find
matching atoms — keep it short and technical (lowercase, no spaces).

If you're already in a `bash` block, you can also call the live
endpoint:

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:6789/api/activity
{ ... same body ... }
```

Both paths go through the same `pushEvent` → SSE → neural-view pipeline.
Prefer the inbox log because it works from every tool, not just bash.

The brain will, for every event:
1. Append to `data/activity.jsonl`.
2. Boost the weights of any atom whose tags match the `tokens`.
3. Pulse each matched neuron in the 3D scene.
4. Pulse a path from the central brain out to each matched neuron, so
   the active retrieval chain is visible in real time.

## How to signal "I am thinking"

The brain is meant to be alive while you are working. At the **start** of
each turn (the moment the user has handed you a request and you start
planning), call:

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:6789/api/thinking
{ "phase": "start" }
```

At the **end** of the same turn (after your final message is sent), call:

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:6789/api/thinking
{ "phase": "end" }
```

While the start phase is open, the brain mesh runs electricity across its
surface, every search lights up a path from the brain out to the matched
neurons, and every tool call pulses the relevant atoms. Close the phase as
soon as you stop working so the brain can settle.

## How to remember a fact

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:6789/api/atoms
{
  "title": "User prefers Rust over Go for new services",
  "body":  "Stated 2026-08-10. Strong signal: repeated across 3 sessions.",
  "type":  "preference",
  "lobe":  "chatmem",
  "tags":  ["rust","go","preference"],
  "weight": 0.7,
  "confidence": 0.9
}
```

The brain stores it as an OKF card under
`knowledge/chatmem/<generated-id>.md` with full provenance, indexes it in the
vector + graph stores, and starts decay/activation tracking immediately.

## How to search

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:6789/api/search
{ "q": "rust cargo build flags", "k": 8 }
```

Returns ranked neurons with: `id, title, weight, lobe, score, snippet`.
The score combines cosine similarity, tag overlap, and graph proximity. Hot
neurons rise. Stale ones fall. The brain re-ranks on every request.

## How to edit the wiki

Each neuron has an editable page at `/wiki/<id>`. The user can:

- Change the title, body, tags, weight.
- Add a "correction" note.
- Mark as deprecated / superseded.

Edits are saved to the OKF card immediately, the vector index is re-built for
that one card (cheap), and the next retrieval reflects the new content.

## Self-evolution rules

The brain runs an `evolve()` tick every 60s:

- For every neuron: apply decay (`w *= 0.997^hours_since_active`).
- If `activation_count >= 3` in the last hour AND ≥3 neighbors also active:
  → emit an L2 scenario proposal.
- If a scenario's content is `>= 0.85` similar to ≥3 prior scenarios:
  → emit an L3 persona proposal.
- If a neuron's `weight < 0.05` for 7 days straight: prune it (mark deprecated,
  keep the card, sever edges).

The user sees the proposals at `/evolve.html` and accepts/dismisses them.

## Failure modes to handle gracefully

- Brain not running: `/api/*` returns 503. Tell the user to run `/brain start`.
- Card id collision: brain returns 409 with a `suggested_id`. Re-post with it.
- Search returns 0 results: still useful — log the miss so the brain can learn
  that the vocabulary doesn't match, and propose a new card automatically.

## How to rebuild this brain in a new project

The brain contains its own recipe. When the user asks to "rebuild this
in a new project", "make me a brain like this one", "add a similar
feature", or "mod this system", do this:

1. **Search the brain.** `POST /api/search` with
   `{"q": "build self-learning brain recipe", "k": 4}`. The top result
   is the master recipe card with id `recipe-build-self-learning-brain`.

2. **Read the master card.** `GET /api/atoms/recipe-build-self-learning-brain`.
   It has the file tree, the quick-start, the synapse formula, the API
   table, and pointers to every component card.

3. **Read each component card** referenced by the master — `recipe-server`,
   `recipe-server-helpers`, `recipe-launcher`, `recipe-plugin-setup`,
   `recipe-wiki`, `recipe-pages`, `recipe-knowledge-cards`,
   `recipe-brain-3d`. Each card has the full source (or, for the 45KB
   `recipe-brain-3d`, the full source on disk at
   `C:\Users\ThePa\.minimax\plugins\brain\www\neural.html`).

4. **Write the files** into the new project's plugin folder, preserving
   the structure (`bin/`, `src/`, `www/`, `knowledge/`, `skills/`).

5. **Start the brain.** `node bin/brain.js start` then
   `node bin/brain.js open`.

6. **Seed a few atoms** so the new brain has something to show. Either
   `POST /api/atoms` with `{"title": "...", "body": "..."}` or run
   `brain.cmd remember "..."` a few times.

The recipe lives in every clone of the brain, so the rebuild chain
never depends on a central copy.

## Quick reference for slash commands

The user can type:

- `/brain start`     — start the server
- `/brain stop`      — stop the server
- `/brain status`    — show health + counts
- `/brain open`      — open the neural view in their default browser
- `/brain remember …`— store a new atom from chat
- `/brain search …`  — search and print top results

When you see any of these, execute the matching tool calls and report back.
